title: test: keystore corruption and partial-write recovery
description:
The keystore AES-GCM file has never been stress-tested for corruption recovery. A partial write (process killed mid-write, disk full, power loss) will produce a file that passes the file-exists check but fails AES-GCM authentication.

Write tests in test/wp11_test_keystore.c:

Test 1 — truncated file:
- Write a valid keystore, then truncate it to various lengths (0, 1, half, almost-full)
- Attempt wp11_keystore_load on each truncated file
- Success criterion: returns WP11_KEYSTORE_ERR_IO or WP11_KEYSTORE_ERR_BAD_PIN (auth fail), never crashes or returns partial key data

Test 2 — bit-flipped ciphertext:
- Write a valid keystore, flip single bits at offsets: header, IV, ciphertext body, auth tag
- Attempt load with correct PIN
- Success criterion: always returns WP11_KEYSTORE_ERR_BAD_PIN (GCM auth fail), never returns decrypted data

Test 3 — wrong PIN on valid keystore:
- Write keystore with PIN 'correct'
- Load with PIN 'wrong'
- Success criterion: WP11_KEYSTORE_ERR_BAD_PIN, no key data accessible

Test 4 — concurrent write + read:
- Thread A: wp11_keystore_create() (writes new keystore)
- Thread B: wp11_keystore_load() on the same path simultaneously
- Success criterion: Thread B gets either a valid keystore or WP11_KEYSTORE_ERR_IO — never partial/corrupt data
- This is a TOCTOU test for the file operations

Test 5 — O_TRUNC race (write-to-existing):
- Write keystore, then call wp11_keystore_create() again (simulates PIN change)
- Success criterion: either old or new keystore is coherent; no intermediate state is readable

All tests must verify that no key material is accessible after a failed load — check that the out parameter is NULL or zeroed.
